posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
You can find more online (note that before 2015, RM2k(3) tilesets were called "chipsets"), but make sure to check the license and don't use rips from commercial games.
One example would be the ones in the ORTP-REANIMATED project
here
(click the "Die Chipset-Sammlung" spoiler tag to get
several tilesets
- but in one file that you have to first split into multiple!!! - and note this thread has 59 pages!), however this one uses the CC BY-NC-SA license so you cannot use them commercially without talking with the authors, but for a hobby project it's fine.
You can also look at First Seed Material / REFMAP assets, see
here
and
here
. Also check out these
asset packs
by final boss blues which you could assemble into tilesets.

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
Fellow RM2K3 enthusiast here.
That chipset is from the RM2K3 RTP I believe, possibly from RM2K (not sure).
Chara-project
website has a complete resource section with assets that are from the RM2K/RM2K3 era. However everything available on that site falls under CC BY-NC 4.0 licensing, and many of the chipset/tilesets are rips from other commercial games. So I'd follow
@Cherry
advice. I'm not sure how acceptable that site is, so I'm not sharing the link. I'm mostly bringing this up, in case your search efforts find you there.
In my experience - asset generation, distribution, and accreditation was a bit of a wild west back then. A lot of free assets you'll find, are derivatives of derivatives, so giving credit to the true source will be a challenge. After a 10 year hiatus, I picked my own project back up. A large part of my time is now sourcing all the assets I collected in my younger (more naive) days. These efforts are largely in thanks to people I've met here, and pixel artists I've talked to.
If you're looking for paid-assets in the retro SNES style, I'd recommend the following
Final Boss Blues
Mana Seed
Using original content is a great way to support the pixel artists out there, it also gives peace-of-mind on licensing. If you have the budget, I'd highly recommend. Just be mindful of AI-generated content. Some artists have licenses that prohibit including their work in projects that also use AI.
I'm new here, so please take my comments with a grain of salt, and adhere to the advice of more experienced members.
I hope this helps
